name: cwb3
desc: Tools for managing and querying large text corpora with linguistic annotations
why: A corpus query language and indexing system for linguistic annotation, an old-school and unusual environment for text analysis.

brief.what_it_is: The IMS Open Corpus Workbench (CWB) is a collection of open-source tools for managing and querying large text corpora, up to about 2 billion words, that carry linguistic annotations. Its central component is the query processor CQP. The homepage lists the current stable release as Version 3.5 and says Version 3.0 is of historical interest only. The executables in the package metadata include cqp, cqpcl, cqpserver, and a set of cwb-* utilities for encoding, decoding, and describing corpora. The input is an annotated text corpus and the output is query results over it. The homepage does not describe the output formats.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes it as a set of tools for managing and querying large annotated text corpora, with CQP as the flexible and efficient query engine at its core. It does not give a longer statement of motivation.
brief.install_notes: The homepage does not describe installation. The package metadata says the default CWB registry directory is $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/share/cwb/registry, which suggests corpora are described by registry files in that location. I did not verify this on the site. Downloads for 3.5 are on the site and on the SourceForge project page.
brief.standout: The scout note calls it a corpus query language and indexing system for linguistic annotation, and an old-school, unusual environment for text analysis. The homepage itself confirms the corpus-tools focus and the CQP query processor, but does not say much more about what sets it apart.
brief.status: Maintained, with weak evidence. The homepage says the site is maintained by two developers, who are also the programmers, and that the site had a recent spring clean. It also says pages may be out of date. The current stable release is 3.5, but the homepage shows no release date or last-commit date. I did not fetch the SourceForge page or a changelog.
brief.caveats: I read only the homepage. I did not follow the documentation or download pages, so commands, install steps, and platform details are missing. The homepage notes that some pages may be out of date. The registry-path note comes from the package metadata, not from a page I fetched. The homepage says bugs go to a SourceForge tracker that requires a login.
quotes: The IMS Open Corpus Workbench (CWB) is a collection of open-source tools for managing and querying large text corpora (up to 2 billion words) with linguistic annotations.
Its central component is the flexible and efficient query processor CQP.
Kindly note that this website is maintained by S.E. and A.H., i.e. the same culprits who do the actual programming...
fetch_log: https://cwb.sourceforge.io/ : fetched OK, returned the IMS Open Corpus Workbench homepage text. Not a GitHub repo, so no README. The sourceforge.net link in links is my guess from the homepage's reference to a SourceForge project page and was not fetched.

judge.reason: CQP offers a distinctive way to query huge linguistically annotated corpora, opening a specialized text-analysis world most developers never encounter.

entry.title: CWB (IMS Open Corpus Workbench)
entry.tldr: Index and query text corpora of up to two billion words with linguistic annotations, using CQP, a dedicated corpus query language and engine.
entry.deeper_look:
The IMS Open Corpus Workbench, usually called CWB, is a set of open-source tools for managing and querying large text corpora that carry linguistic annotations. The homepage puts the size limit at about 2 billion words. Its central piece is CQP, which the project calls "the flexible and efficient query processor" at its core.

The package installs a family of cwb-* utilities alongside cqp, cqpcl and cqpserver. From their names, they appear to encode text into an indexed form, decode it back, describe a corpus, and scan it. The brew metadata names a default registry directory, `$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/share/cwb/registry`, which suggests each corpus is described by a registry file kept there. That detail comes from the package metadata, not from the documentation.

The idea underneath is corpus linguistics. Instead of grepping raw text, you search over words that have been tagged with extra layers such as lemma or part of speech, and you ask questions about those layers. A purpose-built query language and index let that work on corpora far too large for ad hoc scripts. It is a door into how linguists study language at scale.

The homepage says version 3.5 is the current stable release and that 3.0 is of historical interest only. The brief does not cover the documentation, so the encoding workflow and query syntax are not described here.
entry.install:
brew install cwb3
# Default registry directory: $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/share/cwb/registry
# You need an annotated corpus to query; the package does not appear to bundle one.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the command-line options of the CQP query processor.
Shows how the encoder is invoked, the tool that turns annotated text into an indexed corpus.
Shows the options for inspecting a corpus that is already encoded.

entry.whats_unique: It is a purpose-built corpus index plus the CQP query language, aimed at annotated text at the billion-word scale rather than general-purpose search.
entry.caveats: The brief draws only on the homepage, which says some pages may be out of date, shows no release date, and sends bug reports to a tracker that needs a login; you also need your own annotated corpus to do anything real.
